references.text: All who received him, he gave the right to become children of God – those who believe in his name (John 1:12). The expression "believe in his name" (εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ) is identical in both verses and links the content of faith to Jesus' person.

Nicodemus came to Jesus and said, "We know that you are a teacher who has come from God. For no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with him" (John 3:2). This confirms that many saw Jesus' signs in Jerusalem during the Passover festival and were convinced by them.

When Jesus came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him because they had seen all that he had done in Jerusalem during the feast (John 4:45). This points directly back to the signs Jesus performed at Passover in Jerusalem.
A large crowd followed Jesus because they saw the signs he was performing on the sick (John 6:2). This reflects the pattern where people are drawn by Jesus' signs.

Many in the crowd came to believe in Jesus and said, "When the Messiah comes, will he do more signs than this man has done?" (John 7:31). Here we see again the pattern of people believing because of the signs Jesus performed.
Many of the Jews who had come to Mary and seen what Jesus did came to believe in him (John 11:45). Here too, seeing Jesus' signs (the raising of Lazarus) led to faith.

Even though Jesus had performed so many signs before their eyes, they still did not believe in him (John 12:37). This contrasts with those who believed because of the signs and shows that sign-based faith was not always lasting or genuine.

Jesus performed many other signs that are not written down in this book, but these are written so that you may believe (John 20:30-31). The Gospel of John explains the purpose of the signs – to lead to faith in Jesus' name – which corresponds with the wording about believing "in his name."

The Passover commandment in Deuteronomy 16:16 requires all men in Israel to appear before the Lord three times a year, including at the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Passover). This is the background for why Jesus and the crowd were in Jerusalem during the Passover festival.

Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone and needed no one to testify about anyone, for he himself knew what was in man (John 2:24-25). The immediate continuation shows that Jesus did not trust the sign-based faith described, thus qualifying what kind of faith it was.
